intelligence.human_view: Glow is the one thing the machine always overdoes — and "more glow" was the answer to everything until tonight. Just enough is the correction: the underglow underneath is beautiful, and anything more than that is not beautiful. The board itself is obsidian black — no purple on it, no wash over it, no haze — and the only light is the restrained rim around the edge, a perfect amount. Restraint is the beauty: the light frames the object instead of covering it, and the object gets to be black, real, and still. This is the glow law (SN-3180) finished: not just "never over the top," but "only underneath, only around the edge, only just enough." The amount is the law now, not just the direction — and the amount is perfect, which means small.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a beautiful black board, like a shiny piece of night — and just a tiny bit of light glowing underneath it, like a night-light under a bed, and a thin bright line all around its edge. That is beautiful. But if you pour purple glowing paint all over the board, it stops being beautiful. Just a little light, in the right places, is perfect.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, a little glow underneath is lovely — like a soft light under a beautiful black board, with just a thin bright line around its edge. But any more than that is not beautiful at all. The purple glow comes right off the boards themselves — they stay deep obsidian black — and only the smallest perfect amount of light stays, around the edge. Restraint is what makes it beautiful.
intelligence.naya_view: JUST ENOUGH GLOW — UNDERGLOW UNDERNEATH ONLY. ANYTHING MORE IS NOT BEAUTIFUL. THE BOARDS ARE OBSIDIAN BLACK AND LIGHT UP AROUND THE EDGE, JUST A PERFECT AMOUNT.
